messages:
Evan P: hey team, day 1 — i have a corp mac with VMware Fusion running a linux dev VM. host (mac) can reach internal Vault at 10.12.7.11 when on the VPN, but inside the VM i get timeout. any tips? :confused:
Zoe L: welcome! is your VM network set to NAT or bridged? with VPN on the host and NAT on the VM, the guest often won't see host VPN routes.
Evan P: it's NAT (the default). i can ping 192.168.65.2 (the host interface for the VM) from the VM. host can `curl http://10.12.7.11/v1/sys/health` -> 200. VM curl times out.
Sam M: NAT means guest traffic is SNATed by the host. If the VPN client only pushes routes on the host stack, the NAT gateway might not forward to the VPN. Two options: switch VM to bridged so it gets its own IP on the LAN, or add a host-level port-forward/proxy and point the guest at it.
IT Ops: for a quick workaround, run an SSH local forward on the host that binds to the host IP reachable by the VM and forwards to the Vault: on the mac host run:
```
ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:8200:10.12.7.11:8200 $USER@bastion.redwood.com
```
then from VM `curl http://<host-ip>:8200/v1/sys/health`. Replace <host-ip> with the host's NAT interface (e.g., 192.168.65.2) or use `host.docker.internal` equivalent for VMs.
Evan P: tried that but binding to 127.0.0.1 didn't accept connections from the VM. when i change to `-L 0.0.0.0:8200:10.12.7.11:8200` it accepts, but ssh warns about binding to all interfaces. is that safe?
Zoe L: `0.0.0.0` will listen on all host interfaces — fine for short debugging if your laptop firewall is on and you trust the network. better: bind explicitly to the VM-facing address: `-L 192.168.65.2:8200:10.12.7.11:8200`.
Sam M: alternative (no ssh) — use `socat` on the host to forward a host IP:8200 to the Vault, e.g.:
```
sudo socat TCP-LISTEN:8200,bind=192.168.65.2,fork TCP:10.12.7.11:8200
```
then VM can hit 192.168.65.2:8200.
IT Ops: long term, set VM to bridged networking or request a static IP on corp wifi so the VM can be on the same network and pick up VPN routes. Also check AnyConnect/Cisco split-tunnel policy — if your client blocks local LAN access for security, use the bastion jump/proxy instead.
Evan P: switched to bridged, VM got 10.0.1.23 and `curl http://10.12.7.11/v1/sys/health` works now. one more Q: how do i configure `VAULT_ADDR` in my dev container inside the VM?
Zoe L: point it to the forwarded host IP or the internal IP if VM can reach Vault directly. example in shell: `export VAULT_ADDR=http://10.12.7.11:8200` or for forwarded: `export VAULT_ADDR=http://192.168.65.2:8200`.
Evan P: thanks!! switching to bridged fixed it. appreciate the fast help :tada:
infra-bot: ticket INF-5123 created to add a "VM NAT + VPN" troubleshooting note to onboarding docs (assigned eng-infra).
Sam M: we'll add a small note to new-hires: "If using VMware/VirtualBox with host VPN, prefer bridged networking or use host port forward via ssh/socat."
Evan P: saved me — super helpful :heart:
